prompt: Write a textstat package: textstat/__init__.py re-exporting top_words and reading_level from textstat/words.py, textstat/stopwords.py holding STOPWORDS (the, a, an, and, or, of, to, in, on, did, not), and textstat/words.py where top_words(text, limit) counts lowercased alphabetic tokens that are not stopwords and returns the top `limit` (count, word) pairs ordered by descending count then alphabetically, and reading_level(text) bands the mean words per sentence into 'simple' (below 4), 'medium' (below 10) or 'complex'.

setup.test_textstat.py:
from textstat import reading_level, top_words

TEXT = (
    "The cat sat on the mat. The dog did not sit. "
    "A bird flew past the window and the cat did sleep."
)


def test_top_words_drops_stopwords_and_breaks_ties_alphabetically():
    assert top_words(TEXT, 3) == [("cat", 2), ("bird", 1), ("dog", 1)]


def test_top_words_edge_cases():
    assert top_words("", 3) == []
    assert top_words("cat cat dog", 1) == [("cat", 2)]


def test_reading_level_bands():
    assert reading_level("One two three. Four five.") == "simple"
    assert reading_level("One two three four five. Six seven eight.") == "medium"
    assert reading_level("One two three four five six seven eight nine ten.") == "complex"
    assert reading_level("") == "simple"
